Palmitic acid is a long-chain saturated fatty acid (16 carbons), which yields about 9 kcal/g when oxidized.  
Glucose yields about 4 kcal/g.  
Leucine, as an amino acid, yields about 4–5 kcal/g when oxidized (but some energy is lost in nitrogen excretion).  
Alcohol (ethanol) yields about 7 kcal/g.  

Thus, per gram, palmitic acid releases the most energy upon complete oxidation.

Final answer: (B)
